concepts.name: Legal Basis of Inflation Targeting: RBI Act Amendment 2016
key_dimensions: Amendment to Section 45ZA of RBI Act, 1934 — which section was amended and what it mandates
Role of Central Government vs RBI in setting the inflation target (Government sets target, RBI achieves it)
Distinction between the legal framework and the actual operational mechanism
UPSC trap: Inflation target is set by the Government in consultation with RBI — NOT by RBI alone

concepts.name: Flexible Inflation Targeting (FIT) Framework: Definition and Structure
key_dimensions: Meaning of 'flexible' — primary objective is price stability, but growth is a secondary objective
Difference between strict inflation targeting vs flexible inflation targeting
How FIT differs from earlier multiple-indicator approach used by RBI
Why India chose FIT over exchange rate targeting or nominal GDP targeting

concepts.name: Inflation Target: Numeric Value, Tolerance Band, and Review Mechanism
key_dimensions: Current target: 4% CPI inflation with ±2% tolerance band (i.e., 2%–6% range)
5-year review clause — Government reviews and notifies the target every 5 years
UPSC trap: The tolerance band is NOT a target range; 4% is the midpoint target
First target set for 2016–2021, renewed for 2021–2026 at the same 4% ± 2%

concepts.name: Choice of CPI as the Headline Indicator
key_dimensions: CPI-Combined (CPI-C) used — covers both rural and urban consumers
Why CPI preferred over WPI: better reflects retail prices and household cost of living
Urjit Patel Committee recommendation to shift from WPI to CPI as the nominal anchor
UPSC trap: WPI is still used for measuring producer-level inflation but is NOT the target variable under FIT

concepts.name: Monetary Policy Committee (MPC): Composition and Appointment
key_dimensions: 6-member committee: 3 from RBI (Governor as Chair, Deputy Governor, one RBI officer) + 3 external members appointed by Government
UPSC trap: RBI Governor has a casting vote in case of a tie — NOT a double vote
External members' tenure: 4 years, not eligible for reappointment
Quorum requirement: minimum 4 members must be present

concepts.name: MPC Decision-Making Process and Voting
key_dimensions: Each member has one vote; decision by majority; Governor has casting vote in tie
Each member must publicly explain their vote — principle of individual accountability
Meetings held at least 4 times a year (currently 6 times); schedule pre-announced
UPSC trap: MPC only decides the policy repo rate — not CRR, SLR, or other instruments

concepts.name: Failure of Inflation Target: Definition and Accountability Mechanism
key_dimensions: Failure defined as: inflation remaining outside 2%–6% band for three consecutive quarters
On failure, RBI must submit a report to Government explaining reasons and remedial actions
UPSC trap: There is no penal provision against RBI Governor — only a reporting obligation
Comparison with other countries: Bank of England writes a letter to Chancellor; India has a formal report mechanism

concepts.name: Urjit Patel Committee (2014): Recommendations and Legacy
key_dimensions: Expert Committee to Revise and Strengthen the Monetary Policy Framework (Jan 2014)
Key recommendations: CPI as nominal anchor, 4% target, MPC structure, flexible inflation targeting
Distinction: Urjit Patel Committee recommended MPC; earlier Deepak Mohanty Committee also discussed monetary framework
Legacy: Most recommendations were accepted and codified in RBI Act Amendment 2016

concepts.name: Repo Rate as the Primary Instrument under FIT
key_dimensions: Repo rate is the key policy rate — signals monetary policy stance
Transmission mechanism: repo rate → bank lending rates → aggregate demand → inflation
UPSC trap: MPC decides repo rate, but CRR and SLR are decided by RBI separately
Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) corridor: MSF rate (repo+25bps), SDF rate (repo-25bps) form the corridor

concepts.name: Monetary Policy Transmission: Channels and Lags
key_dimensions: Key channels: interest rate channel, credit channel, exchange rate channel, asset price channel
Long and variable lags — policy changes take 3–4 quarters to fully affect inflation
Structural impediments in India: administered interest rates, sticky bank lending rates, cash-dominated economy
MCLR (Marginal Cost of Funds based Lending Rate) and EBLR (External Benchmark Lending Rate) reforms to improve transmission

concepts.name: Supply-Side vs Demand-Side Inflation and MPC's Limitation
key_dimensions: Monetary policy effective against demand-pull inflation; limited against cost-push/supply-side inflation
Food and fuel inflation (supply-driven) dominate India's CPI basket — challenge for MPC
UPSC trap: MPC cannot control food/fuel prices directly — fiscal and supply-side interventions needed
Core inflation (CPI ex-food and fuel) used as a better signal of demand-side pressures

concepts.name: CPI Basket Composition and Its Implications for Targeting
key_dimensions: Food and beverages: ~45.86% weight in CPI-C — highest component
Housing: ~10.07%; Fuel and light: ~6.84%; Core (misc + clothing + health + education): ~47% approx
High food weight means volatile food prices frequently breach the tolerance band
UPSC trap: Core inflation excludes food and fuel but is NOT the official target variable — CPI-C headline is

concepts.name: Inflation Targeting vs Other Monetary Policy Frameworks: Comparative Analysis
key_dimensions: Exchange rate targeting (pegging): used by smaller open economies; India rejected due to external vulnerability
Nominal GDP targeting: proposed by some economists; not adopted — data availability issues
Multiple indicator approach: used by India pre-2016 — lacked clear accountability
Advantages of IT: transparency, accountability, anchors expectations; Disadvantages: ignores output gap, financial stability

concepts.name: Independence vs Accountability of MPC/RBI under FIT
key_dimensions: Instrument independence: RBI/MPC decides HOW to achieve the target (repo rate decisions)
Goal dependence: Government decides WHAT the target should be (4% ± 2%)
Accountability mechanism: public voting records, minutes published after 14 days, failure report to Government
UPSC trap: India follows 'constrained discretion' model — neither full independence nor complete government control

concepts.name: RBI's Failure Episodes and Political Economy Tensions
key_dimensions: 2022–2023: CPI remained above 6% for three consecutive quarters — first technical failure under FIT
RBI submitted report to Government explaining global commodity shocks, Russia-Ukraine war as reasons
Tension between growth vs inflation mandate — Government often prefers lower rates to boost growth
UPSC angle: Institutional credibility vs government pressure — how FIT framework handles this tension

concepts.name: Role of Forward Guidance and Inflation Expectations Management
key_dimensions: Forward guidance: MPC communicates future policy intentions to anchor market expectations
Inflation expectations surveys: RBI conducts household inflation expectations survey — inputs for MPC
Rational expectations theory: if credible, inflation targeting itself lowers inflation by anchoring expectations
UPSC trap: Managing expectations is as important as actual rate changes — credibility of central bank is key

concepts.name: Relationship Between Fiscal Policy and Inflation Targeting
key_dimensions: Fiscal dominance risk: high fiscal deficits can undermine monetary policy by forcing monetization
FRBM Act and fiscal consolidation as complementary to inflation targeting
Coordination failure: if government runs expansionary fiscal policy, MPC may need to raise rates — contradictory signals
UPSC trap: FIT framework assumes fiscal discipline — without FRBM compliance, inflation target becomes harder to achieve

concepts.name: Global Comparisons: Inflation Targeting Across Countries
key_dimensions: Pioneer: New Zealand (1990) was first country to formally adopt IT; followed by Canada, UK, Australia
Advanced economies: US Fed uses Average Inflation Targeting (AIT) — allows temporary overshoot
Emerging market experience: Brazil (3.5%), South Africa (3–6%), India (4% ±2%) — higher targets reflect structural realities
UPSC trap: IMF and BIS generally support IT for emerging markets — but note that China does NOT follow IT framework

concepts.name: Limitations and Criticisms of India's FIT Framework
key_dimensions: Structural criticism: high food weight makes CPI volatile and supply-shock prone — beyond monetary policy control
Growth sacrifice ratio: tightening to control inflation can slow growth and employment (Okun's trade-off)
Financial stability ignored: FIT focused on consumer prices — does not explicitly target asset price bubbles
Criticism by some economists (e.g., Arvind Subramanian): real interest rates remained too high under FIT, hurting investment

concepts.name: MPC Minutes, Transparency Norms, and Information Architecture
key_dimensions: Minutes of MPC meeting published 14 days after the resolution — individual votes and statements disclosed
Monetary Policy Report (MPR): published twice a year — contains inflation projections and macroeconomic assessment
Fan chart: RBI uses probabilistic fan chart to show inflation forecast uncertainty — international best practice
UPSC trap: MPC minutes are NOT released immediately after the meeting — 14-day lag is deliberate to prevent market volatility
